en: Oṃ, homage to the Omniscient One!
Oṃ, homage to Dhanvantari!

The compilation of a hundred formulations will be undertaken from this entire medical system, which has assumed its established authority, which has spread far beyond the field of therapeutics, and which is honored by skilled physicians. Yashas 1.
Having examined the characteristics of the causes and the diseases, the physician who knows medical treatment should apply medicines;
for when the body is free from affliction, these medicines become like nectar. (YŚ 2)

One should drink a decoction of chinnodbhava, ambudhara, dhanvayavāsa, viśva, duḥsparśa, parpaṭaka, megha, kirātatikta, mustā, āṭarūṣaka, mahauṣadha, and dhanvayavāsa in cases of fevers born of vāta, pitta, and kapha. (Yogīndra 3)

A decoction prepared with *kṣudrāmṛtā*, *nāgara*, and *puṣkarāhvaya* is recommended even for a fever arising from the three doṣas, when it is characterized by a predominance of phlegm and wind, and is accompanied by dyspnea, cough, loss of appetite, and pain in the flanks. (Yogaśataka 4)

A decoction prepared from *āragvadha*, *granthika*, *musta*, *tiktā*, and *harītakī* is beneficial in fever associated with *āma*, colic, and *kapha-vāta*; it is both digestive-stimulant (*dīpana*) and carminative (*pācana*). (Yogāśataka 5)

One should administer a decoction of grapes (drākṣā), chebulic myrobalan (abhayā), parpataka, ananta-mula (abda), and katurohini (tiktā), along with the fruit of śamyāka, in cases of fever born of pitta that is accompanied by delirium, fainting, vertigo, burning sensation, delusion, and thirst. (Yogashaṭa 6)

One should drink a decoction of *nidigdhikā*, *nāgaraka*, and *amṛtā*, mixed with *pippalī*, in cases of chronic fever, anorexia, cough, colic, dyspnea, weak digestion, facial paralysis, and catarrh. (Yogāśataka 7)

One suffering from thirst, hemorrhagic disorders, fever, and burning sensations should drink a decoction of *durālabhā*, *parpaṭaka*, *priyaṅgu*, *bhūnimba*, *vāsā*, and *kaṭurohiṇī*, saturated with sugar. (Yogāśataka 8)

Having decocted the three fruits, dāruniśā, viśālā, and musta, one should drink the resulting infusion mixed with honey and a paste consisting of a one-eighth part of niśā, when all types of prameha have arisen. (Yājñavalkyasmṛti 1.9)

A decoction prepared with vatsaka, ativiṣā, bilva, udīcya, and musta is beneficial for diarrhea that is accompanied by undigested matter (āma), pain, and blood, even when it has been chronic. (Yogāśataka 10)

One should drink equal parts of ginger, musta, ativiṣā, and guḍūcī boiled in water, for those with weak digestion, for chronic illnesses, for complications of undigested matter (āma), and for disorders of the digestive tract (grahaṇī). YŚ 11.

One should drink punarnavā, dārvī, abhayā, and guḍūcī together with cow’s urine and mahiṣākṣa resin in cases of skin diseases, swelling, abdominal enlargement, anemia, obesity, excessive salivation, and disorders of upward-moving phlegm. (Yogatarangiṇī 12)

A decoction of mustā, ākhuparṇī, phala, and dāruśigru, combined with a paste of kṛṣṇā and kṛmiśatru, destroys worms that have persisted for a long time through both passages, as well as diseases born of worms. (Yājñavalkya-smṛti 1.13)

One suffering from urinary calculi and dysuria should drink a decoction prepared with elā, upakulyā, madhuka, aśmabheda, kauntī, śvadaṃṣṭrā, vṛṣaka, and urubūka, primarily containing aśmajatu and mixed with sugar. (Yājñavalkya-smṛti 1.14)
Having drunk the powders of cardamom, *aśmabheda*, bitumen, and long pepper, stirred with rice-water;
or alternatively, having them taken as a linctus together with jaggery, even one suffering from dysuria who is near death shall live. (Yājñavalkya-smṛti 1.15)

One should drink a decoction of *harītakī*, *gokṣura*, *rājavṛkṣa*, *pāṣāṇabhida*, and *dhanvayavāsaka*, combined with honey, in cases of painful dysuria accompanied by burning sensations, pain, and constipation. (Yogāśataka 16)
One should drink a decoction of vāsā, guḍūcī, and caturaṅgula with castor oil;
by this method, one may conquer entirely, even if it has spread through all the limbs, every disorder arising from blood and wind (asṛgvāta).
Rasāñjana and the root of taṇḍulaka, taken with honey and drunk with rice-water, destroy uterine bleeding of every origin; and bhārgī together with nāgara cures asthma. (Yogaratnākara 18)

A decoction made from castor root, bilva, the two types of bṛhatī, mātuluṅga, pāṣāṇabheda, the three pungents (tri-kaṭu), and radish, mixed with alkali, asafoetida, salt, and urubhṛta oil, should be drunk for pains in the hips, thighs, penis, heart, and breasts. (Yājñavalkya-smṛti 1.19)

Asafoetida, ugragandhā, viḍalavaṇa, dry ginger, cumin, chebulic myrobalan, puṣkaramūla, and kuṣṭha—these, powdered with each subsequent ingredient added in one part more than the preceding, are desired for abdominal tumors, enlargement of the abdomen, indigestion, and choleraic vomiting. (Yogasataka 20)

An equal powder of rock salt (*rucaka*), asafoetida (*hiṅgu*), and great medicine (*mahauṣadha*, i.e., ginger) should be drunk with ginger-water in cases of ailments arising from phlegm (*kapha*) and wind (*samīraṇa*), as well as for pain in the heart, sides, back, and abdomen, and for choleraic disorders (*visūcikā*); likewise, it should be taken with barley-juice in cases of constipation due to feces (*viḍvibandha*). (Yogāśataka 21)

Having burnt *pūtīka* leaves, *gajacirbhiṭa*, *cavya*, *vahni*, and the three acrids (*vyoṣa*) arranged on a bed with a layer of salt as a cushion below, and having ground them into a powder mixed with curd-whey (*dadhimastu*), it should be administered for abdominal tumors, abdominal enlargement, edema, anemia, and diseases of the anus. (Yogasamhitā 22)

A powder made from twice the amount of asafoetida (*hiṅgu*), along with *vacā*, *kuṣṭha*, *suvarcikā*, and *viḍa* salt, taken with warm water, destroys abdominal distension, cholera-like pain (*visūcikā*), heart disease, abdominal tumors (*gulma*), and upward-moving wind. (Yogāśataka 23)

One should drink the powder of śṛṅgī, the three pungents (kaṭutrika), the three fruits (phalatraya), kaṇṭakārī, bhārgī, puṣkaramūla, and the five salts with non-cold water for hiccups, dyspnea, upward-moving wind (ūrdhvavāta), cough, loss of appetite, and catarrh. (Yogāśataka 24)
Having burned the *nādeyī*, *kuṭaja*, *arka*, *śigru*, *bṛhatī*, *snuhī*, *bilva*,
*bhallātaka*, *vyāghrī*, *kiṃśuka*, *pāribhadraka*, *jaṭāmāṃsī*, *pāmārga*, *nīpa*, *agnimantha*,
*vāsā*, *muṣkaka*, and *pāṭalā* along with salt, one should cook the resulting juice.
This preparation with asafoetida and other ingredients is appropriate for treating abdominal tumors, enlargement of the abdomen, and splenic disorders.

A powder made from equal parts of *cavya*, *amlavetasa*, the three pungents (*kaṭutrika*), *tittiḍīka*, *tālīsa*, cumin (*jīraka*), *tugākṣīrī*, and *dagdhadhūma*, softened with jaggery and combined with the three aromatics (*trisugandhi*), is recommended for disorders of the voice, chronic rhinitis, phlegm, and loss of appetite. (Yogaśataka 26)

Having prepared a fragrant pill consisting of one part each of tālīśa, cavya, and marica; two parts of mūla and tugākṣīrī; three parts of śuṇṭhī and three times as much jaggery, one should administer it for cough, weak digestion, hemorrhoids, fever, and pain. (Yogaratnamālā 27)

One should eat this powder made from ginger, long pepper, black pepper, *nāgadalatvak*, and cardamom—increased in sequence from the last upward—and mixed with an equal amount of sugar; it is effective for hemorrhoids, weak digestion, abdominal tumors, loss of appetite, asthma, and diseases of the throat and heart. (Yogaratnamālā 28)
One should prepare pills with equal parts of rock salt, asafoetida, the three myrobalans, yavānī, and the three pungents (vyoṣa), along with portions of jaggery.
By consuming these, even one with weak digestion attains such satiety that he does not eat much, even when food is abundant. (Yājñavalkya-smṛti 29)
Iron filings, *tila*, the three pungents (*tryūṣaṇa*), and *kola*—each taken in equal parts—with an amount of powdered *mākṣika* mineral ore equal to all of them combined;
a bolus (*modaka*) made from these, mixed with honey and taken with buttermilk, is recommended even for cases of jaundice (*pāṇḍvāmaya*) that have long persisted.

One should always eat ginger with jaggery, or black pepper with jaggery, or *pathyā* as the third ingredient with jaggery, or pomegranate, in cases of undigested food (*āma*), indigestion (*ajīrṇa*), diseases of the anus, and constipation. (Yājñavalkya-smṛti 3.31)
A pill should be prepared from the powder of *harītakī*, ginger, and *musta* mixed with jaggery;
held in the mouth, it wards off even advanced, powerful asthma and cough. (Yogāśataka 32)

One should prepare a pill from *vaṭapraroha*, honey, *kuṣṭha*, blue lotus, and parched grain powder; when this well-compounded mixture is held in the mouth, it quickly destroys even intense thirst. (Yogāśataka 33)

A powder of realgar, māgadhika, and long pepper, combined with the sour juice of wood-apple and licked with honey along with parched grain in equal parts, repeatedly overcomes persistent vomiting. (Yogasataka 34)
The juice of *dūrvā* grass or that produced from pomegranate flowers is prescribed as a nasal drop (*nasya*) when blood flows from the nose;
likewise, [the juice] of lac mixed with breast milk or the excrement of flies destroys hiccup. YS 35.

The juice of the *dhātrī* fruit, resin of the *sarja* tree, *pākya*, ground with *sauvīra* alkali, and fermented with that same [alkali], when used as an ointment (*udvartana*), ensures that skin eruptions (*sidhma*) do not recur. (Yājñavalkya-smṛti 3.36)
Dūrvā grass, abhayā, rock salt, cakramarda, and kuṭheraka, ground with sour gruel and buttermilk,
destroy even deeply rooted ringworm and itching through three applications as a plaster.

One should cook oil with *gaṇḍīrika*, *citraka*, *mārkava*, *arka*, the bark of *kuṣṭha* trees, and salts, along with urine; this removes circular leprosy (*maṇḍala-kuṣṭha*), *dadru*, foul ulcers, pain, and *kiṭima*. Yājñavalkya-smṛti 3.8.38.

This Kaṭuka oil, cooked with equal parts of red lead, guggulu resin, rasāñjana, beeswax, and tuttha, forcibly eradicates scabies, whether it be oozing pustules or even dry ones, by means of a single application as an ointment. // YŚ 39 //

Oil prepared with *suvarcikā*, *nāgara*, *kuṣṭha*, *mūrvā*, lac, *niśā*, *lohitayaṣṭikā*, and six times the amount of buttermilk (*takra*), when used for massage, shall alleviate coldness and burning sensations in fever. (Yogāśataka 40)

This [ghee], prepared with the decoction and paste of *guḍūcī*, *vṛṣa*, and *kaṇṭakārī*, should be drunk in cases of chronic fever, cough, colic, dyspnea, impaired digestion, and disorders of the *grahaṇī*. (Yogaratnamālā 41)

This freshly prepared ghee, quickly perfected with the decoction and paste of the leaves of *vṛṣa*, *khadira*, and *paṭola*, and the bark of *nimba*, along with *amṛtā* and *tāmalakī*, conquers erysipelas (*visarpa*), hemorrhoids, skin diseases (*kuṣṭha*), and abdominal tumors (*gulma*).
Visarpa is a specific type of emaciation affecting the entire body and its constituent parts, produced by the aggravated humors (doṣas) located in the skin, flesh, and blood.
Mada is a state of intoxication, a disorder generated by the consumption of liquor.

A patient who carefully drinks this excellent ghee, cooked according to the prescribed method with water and the paste of *amṛtā*, *paṭola*, *picumarda*, *dhāvanī*, *triphalā*, *karañja*, and *vṛṣa*, conquers leprosy.

Then, one should prepare pieces of *kuṣmāṇḍaka* (pumpkin gourd) cooked by the method of boiling, dried, and fried in clarified butter; when the sugar has been fully melted, one should add black pepper, *magadhā* (long pepper), ginger, cumin, and the "three aromatics" (*trigandha*).
This linctus is for children, the elderly, those with wind-disorders (*vāta*), blood disorders, the emaciated, women, and those suffering from wounds.
It is also recommended for those suffering from thirst, coughs, blood disorders, bile, wind-disorders, anal pain, and vomiting.

Having cooked together cow’s urine, sour gruel, and honey with dantī, piṇḍītaka, kṛṣṇā, viḍa salt, dhūma, and kuṣṭha, one should apply a suppository resembling the thumb of the hand, smeared with ghee, into the rectum; it removes pain and distension.

Saffron mixed with sugar and fried in clarified butter should be administered as a nasal drop (nasya) for diseases arising from wind and blood, such as pain in the eyebrows, ears, temples, eyes, or half the head, and for ailments that increase daily. (Yājñavalkya-smṛti 47)
One should prepare a wick from the seeds within the fruits of *pathyā*, *akṣa*, and *dhātrī* in proportions of three, two, and one parts respectively;
with this, one should apply collyrium for excessive tearing and remove even severe inflammation of the eyes. (Yogāśataka 48)

One should apply an external plaster to the eye made of *harītakī*, rock salt (*saindhava*), *tārkṣyaśaila* (antimony), and red ochre (*gairika*), ground with clear water; this is for the purpose of pacifying all diseases of the eye. (Yogāśataka 49)
Lodhra mixed with rock salt, fried in clarified butter, ground with *sauvīra* alkali, and bound in a white cloth—this should be used as an eye-drop;
it will destroy burning, itching, and pain in the eyes. (Yogāśataka 50)
Sea-foam with sugar cures *arjuna*; cow-dung and black *kṛṣṇā* cure night-blindness;
*rasāñjana* combined with the three pungents (*vyoṣa*) cures *pilla*; and *tāpīsamuttha* taken with honey cures *śukra*. (Yājñavalkya-smṛti 51)

This medicinal preparation (rasakriyā), made from equal parts of *puṣpākhyatārkṣya*, white sea-foam, conch shell, *sindhūttha* salt, red ochre, black stone (*śilā*), and black pepper—all ground together with honey—destroys *arma*, *kāca*, cataracts (*timira*), *arjuna*, and diseases of the eyelids (*vartmaroga*). Yājñavalkya-smṛti 52.
Equal parts of musta, uśīra, rajas, yavāsa, marica, saindhava, kaṭphala, dārvī, tutthaka, śaṅkhaphena, nalada, kālānusārya, and añjana,
powdered together and placed in an iron vessel mixed with honey, are recommended.
And in cases of itching, skin diseases, blood disorders, cataracts, and growths such as pilpas and upadēhas.
This collyrium, prepared from equal parts of mañjiṣṭhā, madhuka, utpala, the bark of udadhiphala,
sevyā, gorocanā, māṃsī, candana, śaṅkha, patra, girimṛd, tālīsa, puṣpa, and añjana— all combined in equal proportions— is always recommended for the eyes.
It removes itching, moisture, impurities, tears, blood, pain, pilla, arma, and leucorrhea.
A decoction of mustā, ativiṣā, indra, dāru, kaliṅga, pāṭhā, and kaṭurohiṇī,
prepared with cow’s urine and combined with honey, should be drunk for all types of throat diseases.
One should prepare a pill from *yavāgraja*, *tejavatī*, *pāṭhā*, *rasāñjana*, *dāruniśā*, and *kṛṣṇā* with honey; one should hold it in the mouth for all diseases of the throat. (Yogāśataka 56)

This gargle, consisting of a decoction of *dārvī*, *guḍūcī*, *sumanā* sprouts, grapes, *yavāsa*, and the three myrobalans (*triphalā*), when combined with honey, pacifies even severe inflammation of the mouth. (Yogāśataka 57)

Kuṣṭha, dārvī, lodhra, abda, samaṅgā, pāṭhā, tiktā, tejanī, and pītikā—this powder is recommended as a rubbing agent for the twice-born; it destroys bleeding from the gums, itching, and pain. (Yājñavalkya-smṛti 1.58)

Having cooked oil with sauvīra, fermented gruel, fresh ginger, citron flesh, and the juices [of these], along with guggulu and rock salt, one should pour that pungent oil into the ears for the alleviation of earache. (Yājñavalkyasmṛti 1.59)
Ghee prepared with vāsā, nimba, paṭola, parpaṭa, phala, śrīcavya, dārvī, ambuda, tikta, uśīra, durālabhā, trikaṭu, trāyantikā,
and candana is effective for disorders above the clavicle, as well as nasal and ocular pain and other such ailments.
It is indeed prescribed for skin diseases, fever, abscesses, wounds, pain, and impotence.
Clarified butter prepared with the paste and decoction of dārvī, parpaṭa, nimba, vatsaka, kaṇā, duḥsparśā, yaṣṭī, vṛṣa,
trāyantī, triphalā, paṭola, kaṭukā, bhūnimba, raktā,
and ambuda is highly recommended for the eyes.
In cases of cataracts arising from bile and blood, as well as in diseases located in the upper part of the body.

Oil prepared with white castor root, ugrā, śatapuṣpā, that which arises from flowers (puṣpodbhūta), bṛhatī, and tagara, along with milk, is an excellent nasal medication (nasya) for destroying timira and other diseases of the upper [parts of the body]. (Yājñavalkya-smṛti 62)
One should throw a conch shell that has been burnt by *analaśikhā* fire into a decoction of *muṣkaka* ash;
having boiled it again with that same water, that alkali (*kṣāra*) is used in oil according to this procedure.
One should employ it in cases of corrupted ulcers, ulcerous pain, hemorrhoids, and sinus tracts.
In cases of skin diseases, fistulas, and various chronic ailments of the throat; Yājñavalkya-smṛti 63.

Having cooked oil with liquorice (*niśā*), *yaṣṭīmadhu*, *padmaka*, blue lotus (*utpala*), *priyaṅgu*, *sāvara*, *lodhra*, and sandalwood, together with milk, one should apply it to wounds; it promotes healing and destroys burning sensations. (Yājñavalkyasmṛti 64)

Clarified butter prepared with equal parts of *jātī*, nimba, paṭola leaves, kaṭukā, dārvī, niśā, sārivā, mañjiṣṭhā, abhayā, beeswax, tuttha, madhuka, and seeds of *naktāhvā*— by this, [the disease] becomes characterized by narrow openings, affects the vital spots (*marman*), and causes discharge.
Deep wounds with pus, accompanied by discharge, become purified and heal. // YŚ 65 //

One should employ śirīṣa flower infused a thousand times with its own juice, along with black pepper and white sugar, as an ointment, a drink, or a nasal drop for those rendered unconscious by snake bites. YŚ 66.
One should drink a substantial amount of *taṇḍulīyaka* combined with peacock bile and *kākāṇḍa*;
it destroys all poisons, both stationary and mobile, along with their complications, in no long time.
Oil from sesame seeds, minced meat, molasses, milk, and likewise arka— these, when drunk in equal proportions,
quickly destroy the fierce poison of a rabid dog, just as the wind disperses a mass of clouds, whether the poison has arisen suddenly or long since.
House-soot combined with mahiṣākṣa, vājigandhā, ghee, and taṇḍulīyaka, ground with cow’s urine, is indeed an antidote that destroys all poisons, both stationary and mobile. (Yogācārabhūmi 69)

Māṃsī, sevya, elā, kauntī, jalaja, jalada, śilā, rocanā, padmakeśī, spṛkkā, caṇḍā, haridrā, gadasi, tapalitā, sṛglatā, padmaka, and kaila— these are equal parts; with eight parts of gaura and four parts of ibhakusuma, these are the *vartayas* suitable for all uses.
Those called Candrodaya destroy sorcery, misfortune, demons, fever, and poison.
Siddhārtha, triphalā, śirīṣa, kaṭabhī, śvetākarañja,
amṛtā, mañjiṣṭhā, the two types of rajanī, trikaṭu, śyāmā, vacā, and hiṅgu— this antidote, when ground with goat’s urine, is recommended for the eradication of all grahas.
It destroys the effects of magical spells, insanity, piśācas, and rākṣasas when consumed through drinking and other means.
An incense is prepared from equal parts of cotton seeds, peacock feathers, *bṛhatī*, discarded flower offerings (*nirmālya*), *piṇḍītaka*, cinnamon bark, bamboo,
cat excrement, chaff, *vacā*, hair, snake sloughs, *gośṛṅgī*,
elephant tusks, asafoetida, and black pepper.
It is remembered as the destroyer of afflictions by Skanda, insanity, piśācas, rākṣasas, and the possession of spirits, as well as fever.

With the paste (kalka) of trikaṭu, kadalī, kuṅkuma, granthika, kṣāra, siṃhī, niśā, kuṣṭha, siddhārtha, the two types of yavānī, ambu, śakrāhvaya, white laśuna, phalatrika, uśīra, tiktā, vacā, tuttha, yaṣṭī, balā, lohitākhya, śilā, padmaka, dadhi, tagara, madhūkasāra, priyāhvā, viṣākhya, viṣa, tārkṣyaśaila, cavya, and amara; The output should be only the translation, no additional text. Clarified butter that is fresh and prepared with the urine and water of all [the aforementioned animals] is known as Bhūtarāva; when drunk, it is the supreme destroyer of seizing spirits (grahas).
With *nata*, *madhuka*, *karañja*, *lākṣā*, *paṭolī*, *samaṅgā*, *vacā*, *pāṭalī*, *hiṅgu*, *siddhārtha*, *siṃhī*, the two types of *niśā*, *latā*, *rohiṇī*,
the fruits of *khadira*, the three pungents (*kaṭutrika*), *kāṇḍa*, *dāru*, *krimighna*, *ajagandhā*, *amarā*, *aṅkolla*, *kośātakī*, *śigru*, *nimba*,
*ambuda*, *indrāhvaya*, *gada*, *śukataru*, flowers, seeds, *ambu*, *yaṣṭi*, *adrikarṇī*, *nikumbha*, and *agnibilva*.

Ghee prepared according to the prescribed method with equal parts of the medicinal pastes (kalka), the group of urines (mūtravarga), and properly administered along with all sequential treatments, quickly destroys all types of possession, insanity, leprosy, and fever; it is known as Mahābhūtarāva.

Dārvī, haridrā, the seeds of kuṭaja, siṃhī, and yaṣṭīmadhuka, taken in equal parts, form a decoction that is used for disorders caused by breast milk in infants and for all types of diarrhea, whether caused by a single or all three humors. (Yājñavalkya-smṛti 75)
A decoction and a linctus made from bilva, dhātakī flowers, water with lodhra, and gajapippalī, mixed with honey, should be administered to children suffering from diarrhea. (Yogāśataka 76)

One should prepare a linctus by finely powdering śṛṅgī, kṛṣṇā, and ativiṣā with honey for children afflicted by cough, fever, and vomiting; or one may administer ativiṣā alone with honey. (Yājñavalkyasmṛti 77)

One *kaṃsa* measure of *dhātrī* powder, saturated with its own juice, combined with equal parts of honey and clarified butter, and joined with eight *prasṛta* measures each of *kṛṣṇā*, *āmalaka*, and sugar, should be placed within a heap of ashes.
By consuming this at the end of a year, one becomes free from gray hair and endowed with beauty, complexion, and vitality.
Free from disease, he is endowed with intelligence, wisdom, memory, eloquence, strength, stability, and courage.

Triphalā combined with yaṣṭīmadhu, saindhava salt, pippalī, and sugar, when administered, bestows longevity, is most aphrodisiac, highly purifying, and destroys old age and disease. (Yājñavalkya-smṛti 1.79)
One should lick the powder of *śvadaṃṣṭrā*, *āmalaka*, and *amṛtā* combined with ghee and honey;
thus, becoming virile, firm, and freed from the suffering of diseases, one lives for a hundred years with black hair. (Yājñavalkyasmṛti 3.80)

Nimba oil that has remained in its natural state, when administered as nasal drops according to the proper procedure, and consumed with milk and ghee for one month, destroys even abundant gray hair caused by old age. (Yogāśataka 81)
Gokṣuraka, kṣuraka, śatamūlī, vānarī, nāgabalā, and atibalā—this powder should be drunk with milk at night by one who has a hundred women in his house. (Yogācārabhūmi 82)
Licking madhuka with honey and ghee, one should follow it with milk;
thus, one does not suffer depletion of the bodily constituents and may approach even a hundred women. (Yājñavalkyasmṛti 1.83)

This emetic, consisting of a decoction of yaṣṭī combined with the best salts, mixed with a paste of kaliṅga and kṛṣṇāphala, and taken with honey, should be administered for diseases of the nose, mouth, throat, and ears. (Yogāśataka 84)

Sour gruel boiled with *harītakī* and mixed with the powders of *dantī*, *aṅghri*, *kṛṣṇā*, and *viḍa*, along with *urubūka* oil, is a purgative that should be administered as it is harmless and destroys disease. (Yogasamhitā 85)

A bolus of jaggery mixed with ghee, along with oil, salt, and honey, combined with a decoction of *rāsnā*, *rāṭha* (citraka), the three fruits (*triphalā*), *amṛtalatā*, the five roots (*pañcamūlī*), *balā*, and meat,
and further processed with a paste of *puṣpāhvā* (mustā), *aguru*, *kuṣṭha*, bilva fruit, *phalinī*, and *kṛṣṇā-vacā*.
An enema combined with sour gruel, milk, and urine is beneficial for diseases caused by wind (vāta).
Oil prepared with the decoction and paste of *balā*, perfumed with fragrant substances, and processed with milk, curd, barley-water, whey, and *cukra*;
likewise, oil cooked individually with *sahācarā*, *saraṇyā*, *amṛtā*, and *varī*—these, when used as an unctuous enema (*anuvāsana*), destroy the wind (*vāta*).

One should administer nasal medication consisting of jaggery and ginger, or else long pepper with rock salt, in cases of diseases of the nose, mouth, neck, jaw, arms, back, head, eyes, throat, and ears. (Yogashastra 88)

Parpaṭaka is prescribed as the best for fevers; Pañcāmlika for thirsts; parched grain (lāja) for vomiting; mountain-grown (giri-ja) [śilājatu] for urinary disorders; the juice of dhātrī for [diabetes];
rāsnā for wind-diseases; urine for abdominal enlargements; and pippalī for diseases of the spleen.
In healing wounds, *kṛmihā* is used; for poison, *śukataru*; and likewise for swelling, *guggulu*.
Vṛṣa is recommended for bile disorders, kuṭaja for diarrhea, bhallātaka for hemorrhoids, and gold for poisons;
dāru is for obesity, krimighna for worms, and harītakī is praised for diseases of the spleen.
In cases of eye diseases, they prescribe triphalā; likewise, for all types of pain, garlic (rasona);
for skin diseases (kuṣṭha), the heartwood of khadira constantly; and for all types of cough, nidigdhikā. Yājñavalkya-smṛti 91.
They recommend *śvadaṃṣṭrā* for aphrodisiac purposes, *nāgabalā* and *balā* for chest wounds,
*āmalaka* for rejuvenative therapies (*rasāyana*), and the substance called *śilā* for diseases caused by the possession of evil spirits.
Thus, these well-known formulations prescribed by rule have been declared for the sake of success by the best of physicians.
To show how even one who is not a physician might employ them after seeing these, something more will be stated here once again. (Yogasamhitā 93)
Through fasting, staying awake, loud speech, physical exertion, riding, and the consumption of pungent, bitter, astringent, and dry substances;
through anxiety, sexual intercourse, fear, leaping over obstacles, grief, and cold; and during the onset of the rainy season, the wind becomes provoked.

Pitta becomes aggravated by pungent, sour, alcoholic, salty, hot, burning, and sharp substances; by anger, fire, sunlight, and physical exertion; by dried vegetables, alkaline preparations, indigestion, irregular eating, and meals during the end of the rainy season. (Yogācārabhūmi 95)

Kapha becomes aggravated by sleeping during the day, and by the consumption of sweet, cold, heavy, sour, and slimy foods such as my own flesh, sesame, sugarcane, milk products, unctuous substances, excessive satiation, salty water, and drinks; likewise, it is provoked in the spring season.

Thus, these doshas, whether increased gradually, in pairs, or all three simultaneously, produce various diseases in the body that are beyond counting and manifold in their designations. (Yogācārabhūmi 97)

Experts declare that the functions of Vāyu consist of harshness, contraction, piercing pain, aching, blackish discoloration, bodily distress, breaking sensations, numbness, coldness, roughness, and dryness. (Yogāśataka 98)

Those who know [the nature of the humors] declare that the functions of bile (*pitta*) are: discharge, sweating, burning sensations, fever, foul odor, moisture, maturation, and provocation; as well as delirium, fainting, dizziness, and a yellowish appearance. (Yogācārabhūmi 99)

Experts declare that the functions of phlegm (kapha) are whiteness, coldness, heaviness, itching, oiliness, smearing, rigidity, adhesion, accumulation, and chronicity; as well as sprinkling, congealing, and delayed action. YS 100.
These are the symptoms of all diseases, which have many names and are produced by various causes;
yet there may be a specific condition of their onset by which they come to be designated by different names. (Yogācārabhūmi 101)

They describe the disease associated with *āmadoṣa* as being characterized by laziness, drowsiness, impurity of heart, lack of physical activity, absence of hunger, retention of urine, heaviness of the abdomen, loss of appetite, and excessive sleep. (Yājñavalkyasmṛti 1.102)
[The treatment consists of] unctuous, hot, stable, aphrodisiac, strengthening, salty, sweet, and sour substances; oil, sunlight, bathing, anointing, enemas, meat, wine, massage, rubbing,
oleation, sudation, decoction enemas, nasal medication, pacification, unctuous poultices, and so forth.
This [regimen of] drink, food, conduct, and medicine shall lead to the pacification of wind.
Bitter, sweet, and astringent tastes; cool breezes, shade, and fanning at night;
moonlight, earthen houses, mechanical devices, water, clouds, and contact with the limbs of women;
ghee, milk, purgatives, sprinkling, bloodletting, and medicinal plasters—[these are the remedies].
This [regimen of] drink, food, conduct, and medicine shall bring about the pacification of bile.
Dryness, alkaline substances, astringents, bitter and pungent tastes, physical exercise, spitting, indulgence in women, travel, wrestling, staying awake at night, playing in water,
trampling with the feet, as well as the use of medicinal smoke, excessive heat, head-purgatives, emetics, sudation, fasting, and so forth.
This [regimen of] drink, food, lifestyle, and medicine will conquer even violent phlegm.

One should conquer undigested matter (āma) through fasting, gruels, light food, soups, water, and bitter broths, as well as by means of drying, sudation, digestive treatments, and purificatory therapies both upward and downward. YS 106.

In the seasons of late winter, the rains, and early spring, there is an aggravation of wind; in the end of summer and the heat of midsummer, that of bile; and at the arrival of flowers (spring), that of phlegm. Indeed, these [diseases] manifest according to what has been ordained for them.

In the provocation of *kapha*, emesis is recommended; in disorders arising from *pitta*, purgation; and in those characterized by *vāta*, they prescribe enemas (*vasti*). In cases arising from a combination of these, this treatment should be mixed accordingly.
Vāta is pacified by sour oils and salts along with sweet foods and drinks; likewise, pitta by sweet, bitter, astringent, and cold substances;
kapha by bitter, pungent, dry, astringent, and sharp substances; and undigested matter (āma) attains pacification through fasting.

Having understood this, as well as whatever else has not been stated here, one of no small intelligence should determine for oneself through reasoning the appropriate remedy for diseases; for a treatise provides but a mere fragment of instruction.
By the supreme merit that I have acquired through composing these hundred verses on yoga,
which abound in excellence and serve as a refuge from the various kinds of diseases, may the entire world become free from illness.
